module_summary: opl.cpp is the menu ELF's entry module: it defines most global settings variables, wires each device page (opl_io_module_t in gSourceRegistry) to its GameSource, and rebuilds a page's rows on the IO worker (updateMenuFromGameList, menuDeferredUpdate). menuUpdateHook is the per-frame GUI hook that throttles background device rescans; the error-message helpers publish IO-thread errors to the GUI through a frame hook and a generation counter. deinit/deinitEx/miniDeinit tear everything down for a launch or exit, setDefaults/init/deferredInit run the boot sequence (pads, config, video peek, device init, default page), miniInit is the GUI-less autolaunch init, and setBootDir/normalizeMcBootDir/main resolve the boot folder and dispatch argv autolaunch.

reusable_helpers.name: formatErrorMessage
reusable_helpers.what: expands only %s/%d/%i/%% from a translated format string into a fixed buffer without passing it to printf

reusable_helpers.name: bootPeekKey
reusable_helpers.what: matches one 'key=value' or 'key = value;' settings line and returns the integer value

reusable_helpers.name: setBootDir
reusable_helpers.what: normalises backslashes and splits a boot path into folder and ELF basename (device root kept for 'mass0:X.ELF')

reusable_helpers.name: resolveMcWildcardBootDir
reusable_helpers.what: replaces 'mc?:' in the boot folder with the card slot that actually holds the booted ELF or folder

reusable_helpers.name: oplPath2Mode
reusable_helpers.what: maps a device path prefix (mmce, smb/nfs, udpfs, pfs/hdd, http, massN) to its IO mode

findings.title: init() starts the pads twice at every boot: startPads() result at line 1686 is discarded and the wait loop calls it again
findings.problem: padStatus is initialised to 0 (1668) and the startPads() at 1686 ignores its return, so the while (!padStatus) loop always runs startPads() a second time even when the first call opened every port. PadManager::start() resets padCount_ and, for every port/slot, calls padPortOpen again without a close and re-runs initialize(): mode-table RPCs, padSetMainMode, press mode, actuator align, and up to six waitReady() polls of 25 x 1 ms each. All of that is repeated on the boot path before the config even loads.
findings.fix: Keep the result of the first call: make line 1686 assign padStatus = startPads() (and drop the separate = 0 initialisation at 1668), so the loop only retries when no port opened.
findings.benefit: One full pad bring-up (padPortOpen + initialize) per port saved on every boot; initialize can wait up to 6 x 25 ms per DualShock and ~25 ms per empty port, so roughly 50-300 ms of boot time (INFERRED from PAD_WAIT_POLLS=25, PAD_WAIT_POLL_US=1000, not measured)
findings.evidence: Read opl.cpp:1661-1709 (padStatus=0 at 1668, bare startPads() at 1686, loop 1701-1708 calls startPads() until non-zero). Read pad.cpp start() 1155-1200 (padCount_=0, startOne per port/slot), startOne 1136-1151 (padPortOpen then initialize then waitReady), initialize 188-297 (waitReady at 207/266/270/274/286/294), waitReady 171-186 with PAD_WAIT_POLLS=25 and PAD_WAIT_POLL_US=1000 (pad.cpp:111-112). grep padPortClose: only unloadOne (pad.cpp:1107), so the first session's ports are never closed before the reopen. The time saved is inferred from the poll constants; whether padman's second open is otherwise harmless was not verified on hardware (boot works today, so it does not fail).

findings.title: IO drains poll once per ~0.25 s delay(1) spin: launch/exit sees an empty queue up to 0.25 s late; lwnbdctl's 1000-tick bound is ~4 min
findings.problem: deinitEx, deinit and miniDeinit drain through IoQueue::blockOps, which re-checks hasPending() only after each delay(1), a 0x01000000-iteration NOP spin that opl.cpp:1269-1272 itself puts at about a quarter second. A queued request that ends just after a check is noticed up to ~0.25 s later, on a black Please Wait screen, on every launch or exit that finds the queue busy. The same tick unit makes LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS = 1000 a ~250 s bound, so a stuck request freezes NBD start for minutes instead of failing it.
findings.fix: In IoQueue::blockOps replace delay(1) with DelayThread(10000) (10 ms, yields the CPU) and restate the budgets in that unit: EXIT_IO_DRAIN_TICKS 100, LAUNCH_IO_DRAIN_TICKS 1000, and LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS at the intended bound. Update the unit comment at opl.cpp:1269-1275 to match.
findings.benefit: Up to ~0.24 s less black screen per launch/exit whenever IO is still queued (INFERRED: delay(1) = 16.8M x 4 NOPs ~ 0.25 s at 294 MHz, poll step becomes 10 ms); NBD preflight bound drops from ~250 s to the intended value; no change when the queue is empty
findings.evidence: Read opl.cpp:1257-1277 (budgets 4 and 40 ticks, comment that one tick is ~0.25 s), callers 1328, 1422, 1962. Read ioman.cpp:360-398 (while hasPending(): delay(1), count down timeoutTicks) and 467-476; hasPending() is head_ != NULL (include/ioqueue.h:31) and head_ is unlinked only after the handler returns (ioman.cpp:140-156), so completion is seen only at the next tick. Read util.cpp:941-950 (delay = count x 0x01000000 loops of 4 NOPs). grep ioBlockOpsTimed(1: opl.cpp x3, lwnbdctl.cpp:150 with LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS=1000 (lwnbdctl.cpp:78); menusys.cpp:248 passes 0 and is unaffected. autolaunch.cpp:204 also states delay() ticks are ~0.25 s. Tick length is arithmetic, not measured.
